'''Henry Morgan Ward'''<ref name="Births">"New York, New York City Births, 1846-1909," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:2WWG-V9Y : 11 February 2018), Henry Morgan Ward, 20 Aug 1901; citing Manhattan, New York, New York, United States, reference cn 32514 New York Municipal Archives, New York; FHL microfilm 1,983,307.</ref> (August 20, 1901 – June 26, 1963) was an American mathematician, a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{citation|title=Prof. Ward of Caltech Dies at 61|journal=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=June 27, 1963}}.</ref>

== Education and career ==
Ward was born in New York City.<ref name="Births"/><ref name="Obit">{{cite news|title=Dr. Ward, 61, Dies; Caltech Theoretician|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/28488977/morgan_ward_19011963/ |newspaper=Pasadena Independent |date=June 27, 1963 |page=43 |via = [[Newspapers.com]] |accessdate = February 16, 2019 }} {{Open access}}</ref> He studied at [[University of California, Berkeley]], receiving his BA in 1924. He obtained his Ph.D. in mathematics from Caltech in 1928,<ref name="Obit"/> with a dissertation titled ''The Foundations of General Arithmetic''; his advisor was [[Eric Temple Bell]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=10385|name=Morgan Ward}}.</ref> He became a research fellow at Caltech, and then in 1929 a member of the faculty; he remained at Caltech until his death in 1963.<ref name="wardcol">[http://www.archives.caltech.edu/search_catalog.cfm?results_file=Detail_View&recsPerPage=1&firstRecToShow=2&search_field=Morgan%20Ward&entry_type=NonPhoto&photo_id=&cat_series= Collection Profile: Morgan Ward (1901–1963)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120424100405/http://www.archives.caltech.edu/search_catalog.cfm?results_file=Detail_View&recsPerPage=1&firstRecToShow=2&search_field=Morgan%20Ward&entry_type=NonPhoto&photo_id=&cat_series= |date=2012-04-24 }}, Caltech Library, retrieved 2010-09-12.</ref> Among his doctoral students was [[Robert P. Dilworth]], who also became a Caltech professor.<ref name="mg"/> Ward is the [[academic genealogy|academic ancestor]] of over 500 mathematicians and computer scientists through Dilworth and another of his students, [[Donald Allan Darling|Donald A. Darling]].<ref name="mg"/>

== Research ==
Ward's research interests included the study of [[recurrence relation]]s and the [[divisibility]] properties of their solutions, [[diophantine equation]]s including [[Euler's sum of powers conjecture]] and equations between [[monomial]]s, [[abstract algebra]], [[lattice theory]] and [[residuated lattice]]s, [[functional equation]]s and [[Iterated function|functional iteration]], and [[numerical analysis]].<ref name="l93">{{citation|first=D. H.|last=Lehmer|authorlink=Derrick Henry Lehmer|title=The mathematical work of Morgan Ward|journal=Mathematics of Computation|year=1993|volume=61|issue=203|pages=307–311|doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-1993-1182245-3|bibcode=1993MaCom..61..307L|doi-access=free}}.</ref> He also worked with the [[National Science Foundation]] on the reform of the elementary school mathematics curriculum,<ref name="wardcol"/> and with Clarence Ethel Hardgrove<ref>[http://www.maa.org/news/inmemoriam_archive.html In Memoriam Archive MAA] C. E. Hardgrove was on the faculty of Northern Illinois University from 1950 until her retirement in 1978.</ref> he wrote the textbook ''Modern Elementary Mathematics'' (Addison-Wesley, 1962).

Ward's works are collected in the Caltech library.<ref name="wardcol"/> A [[Academic conference|symposium]] in his memory was held at Caltech on November 21–22, 1963.<ref name="l93"/> ''Ward [[quasigroups]]'' are named after him, following his paper on alternative set of [[group (mathematics)|group]] [[axioms]].<ref>{{citation|first=Morgan|last=Ward|title=Postulates for the inverse operations in a group|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|year=1930|volume=32|issue=3|pages=520–526|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1930-1501550-7|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=Kenneth|last1=Johnson|first2=Petr|last2=Vojtechovsky|title=Right division in groups, Dedekind-Frobenius group matrices, and Ward quasigroups|journal=Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg|year=2006|volume=75|pages=121–136|doi=10.1007/BF02942039|arxiv=math/0701716|s2cid=17528168}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Ward died of a heart attack in [[Duarte, California]].<ref name="Obit"/>
